frictions.title: Price range slider requires sustained drag operation
frictions.description: Adjusting the budget filter requires continuous pointer dragging on a small slider thumb, resulting in repeated unsteady drag attempts and precision difficulty when setting price range limits.

interventions.description: Add direct-entry numeric inputs adjacent to price range sliders to allow setting budget limits without dragging.

The budget filter on the Booking.com search results page is implemented as a dual-thumb price range slider that requires the user to perform a sustained pointer drag to set minimum and maximum nightly rates. In the observed session, this resulted in repeated unsteady drag attempts, micro-adjustments, and prolonged drag holds before the user could release the thumb at the intended value. Users who cannot perform precise sustained dragging movements, or who rely on alternative input methods, are effectively blocked from accurately setting the price range filter and must depend on a single interaction technique that is difficult to control.
interventions.mitigation: Provide direct-entry numeric input fields adjacent to the price range slider for setting the minimum and maximum budget values. These fields should be visually labeled and accept typed values, and updating a field should update the corresponding slider position and trigger the search results to refresh in the same way the slider does. This gives users an alternative to sustained dragging while preserving the existing slider for those who prefer it.

frictions.title: Gmail notification toast auto-dismisses before Undo click
frictions.description: The 'Conversation moved to Trash' toast notification automatically vanished after ~4.7 seconds while the user was actively moving the cursor toward the 'Undo' button, preventing the user from reversing the deletion (WCAG 2.2.1).

interventions.description: Pause Gmail action toast auto-dismiss on hover or extend its visibility duration so Undo remains operable.

The 'Conversation moved to Trash' toast notification automatically dismissed after approximately 4.7 seconds while the user was actively moving the pointer toward the 'Undo' button. The user hovered over the location where the button had been, but the toast had already disappeared, preventing the deletion from being reversed. This short, fixed timeout gives insufficient time to notice and activate the undo control, especially for users who need more time to locate or reach on-screen controls.
interventions.mitigation: Adjust the toast dismissal behavior so users have adequate time to activate 'Undo'. For example, pause or extend the auto-dismiss timer when the pointer hovers over the toast or when keyboard focus is on it, or provide a user-configurable duration for action confirmations. Additionally, ensure the undo action remains available through another persistent location, such as the Trash folder or an 'Undo' item in a menu, so a missed toast does not permanently lose the ability to reverse the deletion.

frictions.title: Filter drawer 'VIEW ITEMS' button fails to dismiss overlay
frictions.description: On the ASOS Men's New In page, clicking 'VIEW ITEMS' in the filter drawer does not dismiss the slide-out overlay panel. The user spent material effort performing corrective clicks and drags across the drawer footer trying to close it.

interventions.description: Ensure clicking 'VIEW ITEMS' in the filter drawer closes the filter overlay panel.

On the ASOS Men's New In page, after the user selects a filter (size M), clicking the 'VIEW ITEMS' button in the filter drawer does not dismiss the slide-out overlay. The user clicked the button twice (at 11.70s and 16.35s) and the overlay remained visible. Subsequent corrective clicks and drag attempts on the drawer footer (17.91s–21.75s) also failed to close it. As a result, the user cannot see the filtered product list and is stuck in the filter drawer, unable to complete their task of viewing the updated items.
interventions.mitigation: Ensure the 'VIEW ITEMS' button closes the filter drawer overlay after applying the selected filters. For example, attach a click handler that removes the 'showOnMobile_C177c' class from the '.filterLayout_uqDo6' element or programmatically triggers the drawer's close button. Also verify that the drag-to-dismiss interaction on the drawer footer works reliably or provide an accessible alternative that dismisses the overlay.

interventions.description: Add role='heading' and aria-level='2' to visual category section headers.

Visual section headers such as 'community' and 'services' are coded as plain links without heading semantics. Because of this, VoiceOver's Rotor heading navigation cannot locate these structural landmarks, forcing the user to traverse dozens of links manually with repeated Shift+Tab key presses. This made navigation highly inefficient and contributed to task abandonment after the user gave up on keyboard traversal.
interventions.mitigation: Add role='heading' and aria-level='2' to the anchor elements used as visual category section headers (e.g., elements currently matching '.cl-link-table > a.heading'), while retaining their link role and operability. This will expose them to assistive technology as headings, populate the VoiceOver Headings rotor, and enable direct navigation to each section.

interventions.description: Hover-revealed navigation menus, such as 'Medical Care' and 'Prime', close as soon as the pointer leaves the trigger or menu area. frictions.title: Hero carousel auto-rotates before magnified reading and click completion
frictions.description: The homepage hero carousel automatically rotates slides every few seconds without pause controls, shifting banner content and links away while the user is reading in a magnified viewport and forcing repeated clicks on carousel arrows to backtrack.

interventions.description: The homepage hero carousel automatically advances slides every few seconds and provides no pause control. With macOS Zoom magnification, the user needs additional time to pan and read a banner and to move the pointer to a banner link or carousel arrow; the slide changes mid-interaction, shifting the content and target away. The user is then forced to repeatedly re-target and click the previous-slide arrow to return to the banner they were reading, making the promotional content unreliable to access and causing repeated failed pointer interactions.
interventions.mitigation: Provide a visible pause/stop control for the hero carousel, stop auto-advance while the carousel or its controls are hovered or keyboard-focused, and honor the user's prefers-reduced-motion setting so slide changes do not occur automatically. This lets magnified-view users read and activate banner content without the content rotating away mid-interaction.

frictions.title: Craigslist category section headers lack accessible heading semantics
frictions.description: Visual category titles across Craigslist (such as community, housing, jobs, for sale) are implemented as plain links without HTML heading tags or ARIA heading roles. When attempting heading navigation, VoiceOver announces 'Heading not found', blocking structural traversal.

interventions.description: Add heading ARIA roles and levels to Craigslist category section headers.

Visual category titles on the Craigslist homepage (such as community, housing, jobs, for sale) are implemented as plain links without heading markup or ARIA heading roles. When a VoiceOver user attempts to jump between sections using heading navigation, VoiceOver announces 'Heading not found', so the user cannot use structural traversal and is forced to Tab through every link sequentially. This makes the page significantly harder to scan and navigate, especially for screen reader users relying on headings to orient themselves and skip directly to relevant categories.
interventions.mitigation: Add proper heading semantics to the category section titles. Concretely, wrap or annotate the existing category-title links with role="heading" and aria-level="2" (or convert them into real heading elements containing the link), while preserving the link's href and focusability. Ensure the heading semantics are applied consistently to all category sections, including any dynamically loaded content, so assistive technology exposes a navigable heading structure for the page's main sections.

frictions.title: Cart Item Remove Buttons Have Undersized Click Area
frictions.description: Cart item remove buttons (.x-item) render as tiny 12-15px cross icons with minimal padding, requiring precision positioning effort across five deletion attempts before emptying the cart.

interventions.description: Enlarge clickable hit area of cart item remove buttons to at least 24x24 pixels.

Cart item remove buttons are rendered as tiny 12–15px cross icons with minimal padding, creating an extremely small click target. In the observed session, the user needed five precision attempts to remove four items, reflecting the difficulty and error-prone nature of interacting with these controls. Users with reduced dexterity, low vision, or using magnification must position the pointer very precisely, and a small miss leaves the item in the cart or triggers an unintended action.
interventions.mitigation: Enlarge the clickable hit area of the cart item remove buttons (e.g., the .x-item elements) to at least 24x24 CSS pixels. This can be done by applying a minimum width and height with inclusive padding, or by adding an expanded click target via a pseudo-element that extends beyond the visually small icon. The visual icon may stay the same size, but the interactive area should meet the target size minimum.

frictions.title: Cart Item Controls Separated Horizontally From Product Labels
frictions.description: Under macOS Zoom magnification, cart item titles on the left are widely separated from remove controls on the far right, forcing repeated horizontal panning across all four item rows to perform removals.

interventions.description: Align cart item remove controls adjacent to product titles to eliminate horizontal panning under magnification.

The cart row layout places product titles on the far left and remove buttons on the far right, creating a wide horizontal gap. Under macOS Zoom magnification, the visible viewport is much narrower, so the user had to repeatedly pan left and right across each row to connect a product title to its delete control. This pan-read-pan-act cycle was repeated for all four items, incurring substantial navigation effort and increasing the chance of losing context or making errors. The layout effectively requires two-dimensional navigation even though the content could fit in a single compact column.
interventions.mitigation: Restructure each cart row so that the product title and its remove control are grouped together within a compact horizontal area. For example, use a flex layout with a small gap where the title and remove button are adjacent, and allow the row to wrap or reflow so the entire row remains visible without horizontal scrolling when the viewport is magnified. This reduces reliance on horizontal panning and keeps the label-action relationship clear.

frictions.title: Auto-advancing hero carousel rotates slides during magnified inspection
frictions.description: The homepage hero banner auto-advances slides every few seconds without pause controls, moving content away while the user attempts to inspect text under screen magnification.

interventions.description: The homepage hero carousel automatically advances slides approximately every three seconds, and no pause/stop control is visible. When a user zoomed in with macOS magnification attempts to read the banner text or inspect a promotion, the slide changes mid-inspection and moves content out from under the magnified viewport and pointer. The user is forced to repeatedly re-locate and re-focus on moving content, making the banner effectively unusable for people who need extra time or magnification to read.
interventions.mitigation: Provide a clearly visible and accessible pause/play control for the carousel, and ensure the carousel does not auto-advance while any slide content is hovered, focused, or otherwise being interacted with. In addition, respect the user's reduced-motion preference by disabling auto-advance when the system or web platform signals reduced motion. If auto-advance is retained, give users a way to pause and resume it that does not require timing-sensitive interaction.

frictions.title: Broken skip link target prevents bypassing header content
frictions.description: The 'Skip to main content' link references '#main-content', but no element on the page possesses that ID. Activating the link fails to shift focus to the main content area, resulting in repeated unproductive activations.

interventions.description: Fix the 'Skip to main content' link by attaching the target ID 'main-content' to the primary page container.

The homepage exposes a 'Skip to main content' link whose href references the fragment '#main-content', but the DOM contains no element with id='main-content'. When the user activated the link with VoiceOver (VO-Space), focus did not move to the main content region; it remained at the top of the page. This was observed across two distinct episodes, with the user re-triggering the link more than ten times before abandoning the attempt. Consequently, screen reader and keyboard users have no working mechanism to bypass the repeated header and site navigation block and must traverse the entire header on every page visit.
interventions.mitigation: Make the skip link's target resolvable and focusable: assign id="main-content" to the element that actually wraps the primary page content (matching the existing href value) and give that container tabindex="-1" so browsers can place programmatic focus on it. Verify after the change that activating the link moves both the DOM focus and the VoiceOver cursor into the main content container rather than leaving them at the top of the document. Where the fragment target cannot be added to the intended container, update the link's href to point at an existing focusable landmark instead, and add an automated check that every in-page fragment link resolves to a real element ID to prevent regressions.

Verify after the fix that activating the link with a screen reader moves both DOM focus and the screen-reader cursor past the header blocks. As a safeguard, attach a handler on the skip link that resolves the target and calls focus() on it, and add a regression check (unit or end-to-end) asserting that every in-page fragment link on the homepage resolves to an existing element.

frictions.title: When2Meet availability grid slots lack ARIA semantics and focusability
frictions.description: Interactive time slot cells in the scheduling grid are unsemantic div elements lacking ARIA roles, tabindex, and accessible names. VoiceOver and keyboard navigation skip all slots, leaving only static time labels exposed, preventing nonvisual users from marking availability.

interventions.description: Expose availability grid slots as operable controls with accessible date and time names and keyboard support.

The interactive time slot cells in the availability grid are implemented as generic div elements that carry no ARIA role, no accessible name, and no tabindex, and are activated only through pointer/mouse handlers. As observed, Tab and Shift+Tab skipped the entire grid (focus jumped from timezone options to PayPal controls and Safari toolbar items), and VoiceOver could only reach and read the static time/date text labels; VO+Space on those labels performed no selection. The consequence is that a screen reader or keyboard-only user cannot mark any availability at all, which makes the site's core function unusable nonvisually. The absence of role and name also means that even if focus reached a cell, its purpose and selected/unselected state would not be conveyed.
interventions.mitigation: Make each slot cell a real operable control: either replace the div with a native button or checkbox, or add role="button" (or role="checkbox"/"gridcell" within an appropriate grid structure) plus tabindex so it is reachable by keyboard. Give each cell a programmatic accessible name that combines its column date and row time (for example via aria-label or aria-labelledby pointing at the existing date and time label elements), and expose the selected state programmatically (e.g. aria-pressed or aria-checked) kept in sync with the visual highlight. Bind keydown handlers for Enter and Space to the same selection logic used by the existing pointer handlers, ensure a visible focus indicator is present on the focused cell, and consider arrow-key navigation within the grid so users are not forced to Tab through every slot. If drag-to-select is offered visually, provide an equivalent keyboard path (for example select-start then select-end, or per-cell toggling).

frictions.title: When2Meet availability schedule grid lacks ARIA semantics and keyboard operability
frictions.description: When navigating the event schedule with VoiceOver, time slots in the availability grid cannot be focused, read, or toggled. The slots are unlabelled plain div elements lacking table/grid or button semantics, state descriptions, and keyboard event handlers.

interventions.description: Expose schedule grid slots as keyboard-focusable, interactive elements with descriptive ARIA labels and keyboard toggle support.

The availability time slots in the event schedule grid (the `#YouTime...` div elements) are exposed to assistive technology as generic, unnamed containers. They carry no interactive role, no accessible name, no state information, no tabindex, and no keyboard event handlers. In the observed session VoiceOver skipped all slots during linear navigation, announcing only the adjacent time text, and the Rotor's Form Controls, Landmarks, Frames, Window Spots and Links menus listed no grid controls at all. The consequence is that a screen reader and keyboard user cannot reach, identify, read the current availability state of, or toggle any slot, so the primary function of the page — marking one's availability — is entirely unavailable without a mouse. The person stopped attempting the task.
interventions.mitigation: Make each slot a genuine interactive control rather than a plain div: give each slot element an interactive role (e.g. role="button" or role="checkbox", or replace with a native button/input), add it to the keyboard focus order with tabindex="0", and provide an accessible name that includes the date and time. Expose the availability state programmatically (aria-pressed/aria-checked, or state text included in the accessible name) and keep it synchronised when the slot changes. Bind Enter and Space keydown handlers to the same toggle logic currently invoked by pointer interaction, so the grid can be operated without dragging or clicking, and ensure a visible focus indicator on the focused slot. Additionally expose the grid's row/column structure (native table markup or role="grid"/"row"/"gridcell") so the relationship between a slot, its time, and its day is programmatically determinable, and announce state changes to assistive technology after a toggle.

frictions.title: Sold-out size radio buttons missing accessible disabled state
frictions.description: Out-of-stock size options are visually styled as sold out but VoiceOver announces them as ordinary operable radio buttons without stating availability, leading to trial selection of unavailable sizes.

interventions.description: Expose out-of-stock state on size selection options for screen reader users.

On the product page, size options that are out of stock are distinguished only by visual styling (the sold-out class applied to the radio button container). The corresponding input elements do not expose any unavailable state (no disabled or aria-disabled attribute) and their accessible names do not mention availability, so VoiceOver announced the XS option simply as 'XS radio button', identical to in-stock sizes. As a consequence, the screen reader user selected an unavailable size, and only discovered the unavailability after the page replaced the purchase controls with a sold-out notification form. This forces trial-and-error selection across sizes and makes availability information effectively unavailable to non-visual users.
interventions.mitigation: Expose the out-of-stock state programmatically on the size controls, not just visually: for each radio input whose container carries the sold-out styling, set aria-disabled="true" (or the native disabled attribute where selection should be blocked) and include the availability status in the control's accessible name or as associated text (for example 'XS — out of stock'), so the accessibility tree matches the visual presentation. Also ensure the sold-out state is applied when the markup is rendered and re-applied whenever variant availability updates dynamically, and announce the resulting sold-out message through a live region so the change is conveyed after selection.

frictions.title: Missing heading markup prevents VoiceOver heading navigation
frictions.description: Attempting to jump between sections using the VoiceOver heading navigation shortcut returns 'Heading not found' because visual section titles lack HTML heading elements or heading ARIA roles.

interventions.description: Add heading ARIA roles to visual section titles so VoiceOver heading navigation can jump to page sections.

Visual section titles on the weather.gov home page are rendered as styled text without HTML heading elements or heading roles. When the user issued the VoiceOver heading navigation command (Ctrl+Option+Shift+Cmd+H) multiple times, VoiceOver announced 'Heading not found', so no structural jump points were exposed. As a consequence, the user had to fall back on sequential VO+Right Arrow traversal through long header and regional map link lists to reach content, which substantially increases the number of keystrokes and the time needed to locate a page section, and removes the ability to build a mental overview of the page structure.
interventions.mitigation: Mark up the visual section titles (for example the forecast title element and the main sub-navigation section labels) with real heading elements (h1–h3) reflecting the document's visual hierarchy, or, where markup changes are constrained, apply role="heading" with a matching aria-level to the existing title elements. Keep the visual presentation unchanged, ensure each page region that appears as a titled section has exactly one corresponding heading, and verify with VoiceOver that the heading rotor and heading navigation commands now enumerate these sections.

frictions.title: National Weather Service page lacks ARIA landmarks in VoiceOver rotor
frictions.description: When opening the VoiceOver Rotor to navigate by landmarks on weather.gov, VoiceOver announces 'No items in Landmarks menu' because the page uses generic div elements without HTML5 or ARIA landmark roles.

interventions.description: Add HTML5 ARIA landmark roles to major container elements on weather.gov.

The user opened the VoiceOver Rotor (VO-U) to jump between page regions on weather.gov, and VoiceOver announced 'No items in Landmarks menu'. The observed DOM and accessibility tree show the page's top-level structural containers as generic div elements without HTML5 sectioning elements or ARIA landmark roles, so no programmatic regions are exposed. Consequence: screen reader users cannot use landmark navigation to move directly to the header, primary navigation, main content, or sidebar, and must instead traverse the page sequentially (as observed when the user Tabbed through long runs of map region links) to reach content.
interventions.mitigation: Expose the existing top-level containers as programmatic regions, either by replacing them with HTML5 sectioning elements (header, nav, main, aside) or by adding the corresponding ARIA landmark roles (banner, navigation, main, complementary) to the current div wrappers for the header, top navigation, page body, and sidebar. Where more than one landmark of the same type exists, give each a distinguishing accessible name (e.g. aria-label). Re-test by opening the VoiceOver Rotor Landmarks menu and confirming the regions are listed and navigable. Consider pairing this with a skip-to-main-content link near the start of the tab order so keyboard users can bypass the repeated navigation and map link blocks.

frictions.title: Uber Eats Customization Modal Separates Flavor Labels and Buttons
frictions.description: Under macOS Zoom magnification, flavor labels on the left and '+' increment buttons on the far right of the customization modal cannot fit simultaneously in the viewport, requiring repeated horizontal panning to confirm choices before clicking.

interventions.description: In the item customization modal, each option row places the flavor name at the left edge and the quantity stepper ('-' / count / '+') at the right edge, with a wide empty gap between them. At the magnification level used with macOS Zoom, only one end of a row fits in the visible viewport, so the user repeatedly panned horizontally between the label and the increment button to verify that the quantity being changed belonged to the intended flavor (e.g., setting Lemon Pepper to 5). Consequences: increased interaction cost per selection, loss of the label/control association at high zoom, and a real risk of incrementing the wrong option because the row identity is only conveyed by horizontal alignment that is off-screen when the control is in view.
interventions.mitigation: Reduce the horizontal distance and dependency between an option's label and its stepper control so both remain perceivable together when content is magnified or the viewport is narrow. Concretely: cap the option row's content width (or place the stepper immediately after the label text rather than pinning it to the far right of the modal); allow the row to reflow to a stacked label-above-control layout at narrow effective widths; and ensure each stepper control carries an accessible name that includes the flavor it belongs to (e.g., 'Increase quantity of Lemon Pepper') plus a visible or programmatically associated indication of the current quantity, so the control is self-identifying without needing the distant label in view. Verify the modal at reduced viewport widths / increased zoom levels to confirm no horizontal panning is required to pair a label with its control.

Ensure the modal content reflows without requiring horizontal scrolling/panning at high zoom levels, and keep each control programmatically associated with its visible flavor label so the pairing remains unambiguous when only part of the row is visible.

frictions.title: Flight result row requires horizontal panning under magnification
frictions.description: High macOS Zoom magnification prevents viewing complete flight details (times, duration, stops, emissions, price) within a single viewport, forcing continuous horizontal pointer panning across the wide web layout during flight evaluation.

interventions.description: On the flight search results page, all data belonging to one flight option is laid out in a single wide horizontal row, with departure/arrival times at the left edge and price plus the expand control at the right edge. When the viewport is effectively narrowed by magnification, the row does not reflow into a narrower stacked presentation, so no complete flight option is readable within one magnified view. The user was observed repeatedly panning the pointer horizontally across the same row (segments at ~2.5s-27.2s, 0.4s-29.9s, 0.02s-7.2s) to move between price/expand controls and departure details. The consequence is high interaction cost and increased risk of losing track of which row is being read or of mismatching a price to the wrong itinerary, because the related fields are never co-visible.
interventions.mitigation: Ensure the results list reflows at small effective viewport widths (for example, honor a narrow-width breakpoint so each result stacks times, duration, stops, emissions and price vertically within a single compact card instead of a full-width row), and keep the primary price and expand control adjacent to the itinerary summary rather than pinned to the opposite edge. Verify the layout with the results page at reduced viewport width / high browser zoom so that one flight option can be read without horizontal panning; where a wide table-style layout must be retained, provide a compact or list-density option and repeat key identifying information (route and times) near the price so the fields do not need to be visually joined across the full page width.

frictions.title: Hover navigation menu collapses during magnified pointer panning
frictions.description: The hover-revealed mega-menu collapsed when the pointer panned past its boundary in the magnified view, forcing the user off the navigation menu for a second time (WCAG 1.4.13).

interventions.description: The top-navigation mega-menu ('Men', 'Women') is revealed on pointer hover and disappears as soon as the pointer leaves the trigger/panel region. When the page is viewed with screen magnification, only part of the menu is visible at once, so the user must pan the pointer to read the columns of subcategories. Twice in this session (once for 'Men', and again at 0:15.8 while reading past 'Sunglasses' under the 'Women' menu) the pointer crossed the panel boundary during panning and the menu collapsed without any deliberate dismissal action, leaving the viewport panned over unrelated hero content. The user then has to re-locate the trigger at high magnification and restart the browsing of the category list, making the navigation effectively unusable for reading long, multi-column menus.
interventions.mitigation: Make the hover-revealed menu persistent and deliberately dismissible: keep the panel open until the user presses Escape, clicks/activates elsewhere, or moves focus/pointer away after a short grace period, rather than closing immediately on pointer-out. Ensure the hoverable region includes the full panel plus a tolerance area bridging any gap between trigger and panel so incidental pointer movement between menu items does not dismiss it. Additionally, allow the menu to be opened and held open by click/tap activation and by keyboard focus (with Escape to close), so category browsing does not depend on maintaining continuous hover. Verify the behaviour at high zoom levels where the panel extends beyond the visible viewport.

frictions.title: Kickstarter campaign video lacks closed captions for spoken dialogue
frictions.description: The product video contains spoken dialogue essential to understanding the campaign, but the embedded video player lacks captions or caption controls, blocking text access to audio.

interventions.description: Turn on macOS Live Captions in System Settings > Accessibility > Live Captions to generate real-time captions for spoken computer audio when video captions are unavailable.

The campaign's product video plays spoken dialogue that carries information essential to understanding the project, but no captions were displayed and no caption toggle was present in the player controls. Users who are deaf or hard of hearing, or anyone unable to use audio in their current environment, cannot access the spoken content and therefore cannot evaluate the campaign from the video. Because there is no caption control at all, users also have no way to discover whether a caption track exists.
interventions.mitigation: Supply a synchronized caption track for the prerecorded video (e.g., a WebVTT/SRT track associated with the media element or uploaded through the platform's caption upload path) covering all spoken dialogue and meaningful non-speech audio. Expose a persistent, keyboard-operable and screen-reader-labelled caption toggle in the player control bar, with its pressed/selected state programmatically communicated. Where campaign creators supply the media, prompt or require caption upload during the submission flow and surface a clear indicator when a video has no caption track. As an additional (not substitute) measure, publish a text transcript adjacent to the video on the campaign page.

frictions.title: Kickstarter promotional video lacks closed captions for spoken narration
frictions.description: The embedded Kickstarter video contains essential spoken dialogue without author-provided closed captions, requiring the user to manually switch on macOS Live Captions as an automated fallback.

interventions.description: When video closed captions are unavailable, use macOS Live Captions from the menu bar or System Settings > Accessibility > Live Captions to transcribe spoken computer audio.

The embedded prerecorded campaign video on the Kickstarter project page conveys essential product information through spoken narration, but no author-provided closed captions were available in the player during playback (including full screen). As a consequence, the narration content is inaccessible to users who cannot hear or rely on captions unless they leave the page context and switch on a system-level automated transcription tool. In this session the user moved to the macOS menu bar mid-playback to enable Live Captions, which interrupts viewing and yields machine-generated text that is not synchronized with the player, may misrecognize product names and terminology, and does not identify speakers or non-speech audio.
interventions.mitigation: Ship an author-authored, synchronized caption track with the video (for example a WebVTT track exposed through the player's caption/subtitle control) covering all spoken narration plus speaker identification and meaningful non-speech audio, and make the caption toggle discoverable and operable in both inline and full-screen player states. If the video platform used for campaign embeds supports uploaded caption files, require or prompt for a caption track at upload time and surface a visible fallback such as a full text transcript adjacent to the video on the campaign page so the narration content remains available without relying on system-level speech recognition.

comparison_notes.text: Recall is identical (91.3% vs 43.5%): both systems surface the same 21 of 23 and miss only the Walmart add-to-cart announcement — a dynamic barrier invisible to the static audit and (so far) to GAM. The separation is precision: 91.3% vs 43.5%, ≈0.57 unmatched barriers listed per recording by the audit. Barrier classes that would separate recall (focus management, ARIA that lies about state, silent dynamic updates, reading order) are not yet in the dataset.

The clearest observational advantage: 73.7% vs 21.1% recall. Magnifier-viewport misses, hover dismissal, panning cost, and zoom-conditional layout failures are properties of the interaction and have no markup signature for an audit to find.

Narrow problem space, split verdict: on caption cases the static audit is accurate and terse (precision 100.0%), but it is structurally blind to sound-cue events with no visual counterpart — GAM 50.0% vs 40.0% recall overall.

GAM 33.3% recall at 80.0% precision vs 16.7% at 25.0%. A static audit can name rule-level candidates (it flagged Booking's missing drag alternative, WCAG 2.5.7) but mis-localizes them (on Reddit it flagged small targets on the search close icon — not the upvote controls the user fought) and cannot see friction evidence at all (Gmail time pressure, ASOS accidental activations). Pages typing is a native app — nothing to audit.

The audit enumerates what could be wrong (~0.9 barriers per recording at 37.0% precision); observation determines what actually blocked this user (88.0% precision) and is what makes the n/a columns — intervention mode, personalized repair, evidenced report — possible at all.
